title: Linear-Time Canonical Header Validity Test
statement: For every machine format $F$, there exist a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $a\\in\\mathbb N$ such that, on every Boolean input $\\alpha$, $M$ halts after exactly $a(|\\alpha|+1)$ steps and outputs the one-bit word indicating whether $\\alpha$ has a valid pair parse and its parsed header is canonical, meaning its last bit is true (with the empty header accepted).
hypotheses_covered: output is the one-bit test for successful pair parsing and canonical parsed header
